detailed_rationale:
Inox Green Energy Services provides operations & maintenance (O&M) services for wind assets, historically tied to its parent Inox Wind's installed base. Q4 FY26 showed strong momentum: total income of Rs 120 crore (+40% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 57 crore (+93% YoY), and PAT of Rs 28 crore (+340% YoY), with the O&M fleet maintaining 96.5% machine availability across a 13+ GW portfolio (10.5 GW of it wind). The more structurally important development is the NCLT-approved acquisition (July 27, 2026) of Wind World India's 4.5 GW O&M arm, which generates roughly Rs 600 crore of high-margin recurring revenue -- for Inox Green's portion of this transaction, management has stated the deal is being funded from existing cash balances, i.e. non-dilutive and non-debt-funded. That is a real, completed, cash-funded step-change to the recurring-revenue O&M base (nearly doubling the managed capacity), not a base-effect or one-off gain, and management has guided FY27 EBITDA above Rs 600 crore on the back of it.

Current point-in-time profitability metrics are still modest -- ROE of 1.86% and ROCE of 2.99% -- reflecting that the business is early in translating this scale-up into returns, and the trailing PE of ~70x is rich against those current returns. The quant scorecard's leverage figures are a genuine strength here: debt/equity of just 0.052x, meaning the balance sheet entered this acquisition essentially unlevered, consistent with the all-cash funding description. The model's own 1-year composite score (40.72, Hold) already reflects the recent momentum; only the 3-year score (23.39, Sell), weighed down by the company's historically weak ROE/ROCE years, pulls the blended verdict to Sell.
recommendation_rationale: I am exercising the asymmetric override here (Sell -> Hold) because the combination of a real, NCLT-approved, cash-funded acquisition that nearly doubles the recurring O&M revenue base, an essentially debt-free balance sheet, and genuinely strong recent operating momentum (PAT +340%, EBITDA +93%, 96.5% machine availability) reads better than a Sell. The quant model's own 1-year score (40.72) already agrees with Hold; the 3-year score is dragged down by historically weak ROE/ROCE that predates this scale-up. Current ROE/ROCE are still low and the multiple is not cheap, which is why this is a Hold rather than anything stronger -- the rescue is about avoiding an unwarranted Sell, not endorsing the valuation outright.
summary: Inox Green Energy Services provides operations and maintenance for wind power assets. The business has just completed a cash-funded acquisition that nearly doubles the capacity it manages under long-term O&M contracts, on top of already-strong recent growth in revenue and profit. Current returns on capital are still modest and the valuation is not cheap, but the balance sheet is essentially debt-free and the recent growth is backed by a real, completed transaction rather than one-off accounting items.
positive_para: The Wind World O&M acquisition (NCLT-approved, ~4.5 GW, ~Rs 600 crore of high-margin recurring revenue) is funded from existing cash, not debt or dilutive equity, and nearly doubles the company's managed wind O&M capacity -- a genuine structural step-up, not an accounting artifact. Recent operating momentum is strong (Q4 PAT +340% YoY, EBITDA +93% YoY, 96.5% machine availability), the balance sheet is essentially unlevered (debt/equity ~0.05x), and management has guided FY27 EBITDA above Rs 600 crore on the combined base.
negative_para: Current returns on capital are still weak -- ROE of 1.86% and ROCE of 2.99% -- so the business has not yet demonstrated it can convert its growing O&M base into attractive returns, and a trailing PE near 70x is not cheap against those current metrics; much of the recent PAT growth is also flattered by a small prior-year base. Integration risk on the newly acquired Wind World assets (a distressed-asset acquisition out of insolvency) is real and unproven.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A trailing PE near 70x against ROE of under 2% would be difficult to justify on trailing numbers alone, but this is precisely a case where trailing metrics understate the forward picture: the Wind World acquisition, funded entirely from cash, adds ~Rs 600 crore of high-margin recurring O&M revenue that was not in the base used to compute those trailing returns, and management's FY27 EBITDA guidance (>Rs 600 crore) implies a step-change in earnings power. If that guidance is delivered, current ROE/ROCE should improve materially without any further capital being raised, since the deal was cash-funded -- that is the basis for treating the multiple as forward-looking rather than as a red flag today, while still not being cheap enough to go beyond Hold.
